chapter: Hopkins, Kelly's Stables and Red Allen
title: Claude Hopkins's personnel; leaving to follow Dizzy
summary: Vic Dickinson, Happy Michener and Linc Mills stood out; after nine months he left to follow Dizzy to Teddy Hill's band.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Yes, that was funny. Well, all right. Well, listen, what I ought to just ask you though, who was in that Claude's band? Who were some of the guys?
Well, there was -- let's see. Now there was Vic Dickinson --
Was Vic in the band?
Oh, yeah. He was my running mate.
Oh, yeah. He still blows so beautifully doesn't he?
Yeah. Vic and this fellow I'm telling you about, Happy Michener.
Yeah.
He was in the band. In fact he was the one that recommended me.
Oh.
To Carl, you know, because we had worked
together with Edgar.
: Yeah. Yeah.

And let's see -- there were so many good musicians in that band. And there was a trumpet player, we used to call him Linc. His name was Lincoln [Mills], but everybody called him Linc. He was a fantastic trumpet player.
: Was he.
And those were guys who stood out, you know.
: Yeah.
In my mind.
: Yeah. That's all I'm asking you, really.
Uh-huh.
: Because you know, just who were the guys that come to your memory.
Uh-huh.
: From that time. Well, why did you only stay for nine months?
Well, because Dizzy was with Teddy, so naturally I'm going to follow Dizzy.
: Yeah, that's right.
To the end of the world.
(Laughter)
: Yeah.

Because I thought that Dizzy was the source. I don't know. I felt that the -- jazz came from Dizzy, you know? I felt that he knew everything there was to know that I wanted to know that he knew, so I would just stick to him all the time.
Yeah.
And after that I stuck to him all the time. I would never leave him. As close as I could get to Dizzy, that was where I was.
Is Dizzy --
(End of Side 7)
